title: Ghana Air Force receives Airbus ACH160
summary: This is the second helicopter to be delivered under the government's acquisition program, following the arrival of the Airbus ACH175 in March 2026.
body_markdown:
Ghana Air Force has received a newly acquired Airbus[ACH160](https://helitrader.com/for-sale/helicopters/airbus/ach160) helicopter at the Air Force Base Accra on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, marking another significant milestone in the government’s ongoing efforts to strengthen the Ghana Air Force’s aviation capabilities.


The[ACH160](https://helitrader.com/for-sale/helicopters/airbus/ach160) is the second helicopter to be delivered under the government’s acquisition program, following the arrival of the Airbus ACH175 in March 2026.


Both aircraft form part of the four helicopters the government plans to procure and deliver in phases as part of efforts to enhance the operational capabilities of the Ghana Air Force.


Ghana Air Force Photo


The acquisition forms part of a broader strategic initiative to augment the Ghana Air Force’s existing fleet, enhance operational readiness and strengthen its capacity to effectively discharge its constitutional mandate in support of national security and developmental objectives.


Regarded as one of the most technologically advanced helicopters in its class, the Airbus[ACH160](https://helitrader.com/for-sale/helicopters/airbus/ach160) combines modern aviation technology, impressive flight performance and exceptional passenger comfort.


Its advanced Helionix digital cockpit enhances flight safety and pilots’ situational awareness, while its powerful twin engines and innovative rotor design contribute to improved efficiency, reduced noise and smoother flight operations. The helicopter also features a spacious and elegantly designed cabin, making it well-suited for executive transportation and other designated missions.


Ghana Air Force Photo


The delivery flight commenced from Marignane, France, and followed a carefully planned route through Spain and North-West Africa before continuing southwards along the West African Atlantic coast towards Ghana.


During the journey, the helicopter made scheduled stops in Spain, Morocco, Western Sahara, Mauritania, Senegal, The Gambia, Guinea, Liberia and Côte d’Ivoire before arriving at its final destination in Accra.


Ghana Air Force Photo


As custodian and operator, the Ghana Air Force will ensure the effective management, maintenance and deployment of both aircraft to support executive transportation and other national assignments.


Dignitaries present were the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Vice Marshal Eric Agyen-Frempong, Chief of the Army Staff, Major General Lawrence Kwaku Gbetanu, Deputy Head of Mission, French Embassy, Rafael Pont, representatives from Airbus Helicopters and senior military officers.


*This press release was prepared and distributed by the Ghana Air Force.*
